resolved_by: Sentencing Commission amendment to U.S.S.G. § 2K2.1(b)(4)(B), which the opinion says was adopted to resolve the circuit differences over the meaning of 'altered' (89 Fed. Reg. 36853, 36858–59 (May 3, 2024))
issue: Does the four-level enhancement for a firearm with an altered or obliterated serial number apply when the firearm also bears a separate, legible serial number?

sides.position: The enhancement applies when a single serial number on the firearm has been altered or made illegible, even if the firearm also has a separate legible serial number (pre-amendment reading of 'altered').
cases: United States v. Thigpen, 848 F.3d 841, 845–46 (8th Cir. 2017)
United States v. Craddock, No. 25-2573 (3d Cir. 2026)

sides.position: The enhancement does not apply when the firearm retains a complete and accurate serial number, so a separate legible number defeats the enhancement (defendant's reading, rejected by this court).
cases: United States v. Craddock, No. 25-2573 (3d Cir. 2026)

this_court: The Third Circuit holds that the enhancement applies where a single serial number was altered or made illegible, and a separate legible serial number does not bar it. The court treats the 2024 amendment as having resolved the earlier circuit disagreement.
quote: Sentencing Guidelines for United States Courts, 89 Fed. Reg. 36853, 36858–59 (May 3, 2024) (detailing circuit split).
cite: United States v. Noah Craddock, No. 25-2573 (3rd Cir. 2026)
